title: Nine hundred and fifty years
hook: Nuh calls his people by night and by day, openly and in private, and few listen (71:5–9; 29:14)

segments.voice: Yesterday: Habil, Qabil's brother, the crow, and your line: one life is like all lives. Who did you treat as a whole world? Day twenty-nine.
screen: `HABIL — ONE LIFE IS LIKE ALL LIVES.`

segments.voice: A teacher stands at the front of a room where nobody's listening. Phones out, heads down, someone asleep in the back. She says it again, a different way. And again. Tries a joke. Tries a story. Stays after class in case anyone wants to ask. Almost nobody does. Do that for a lifetime. Then for many lifetimes. Adam's story is behind us. The path moves on to the next great prophet, a man remembered for a boat. But the Qur'an spends whole passages on something else: how long he kept talking to people who wouldn't listen.
screen: `A ROOM WHERE NOBODY'S LISTENING.` → `SAY IT AGAIN, ANOTHER WAY.` → `NUH, BEFORE THE BOAT.`

segments.voice: Nuh. Noah. A whole surah carries his name, surah seventy-one, and it's almost entirely his report to God about his work. Paraphrasing: my Lord, I've called my people night and day, and my calling has only made them run further away. Every time I called them, so You could forgive them, they put their fingers in their ears and pulled their clothes over their heads. I called them openly. I spoke to them in public, and I spoke to them in private. Listen to that list. Night and day. Loud and quiet. Crowds and one at a time. He tried everything. What was he asking? Not much, the surah says: ask your Lord's forgiveness; He is forgiving. And he promised rain, and gardens, and rivers. And then the number. Surah twenty-nine, in Pickthall's words: “he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years.” Nine hundred and fifty years. Scholars have discussed it. Some take it as it stands. Others note it describes how long he stayed among his people, and differ over how it fits his whole life. Either way, the point is plain: a stretch of patience almost too long to imagine. And the result? The Qur'an is honest: only a few believed with him. By the world's measure, it looks like failure. But a hadith in Bukhari, about the Day of Judgment, has people coming to Nuh and calling him the first messenger to the people of the earth, and a grateful servant. His success wasn't counted in listeners. It was counted in the calling.
screen: `MY LORD, I'VE CALLED THEM NIGHT AND DAY.` · `FINGERS IN THEIR EARS.` · `A THOUSAND YEARS SAVE FIFTY.` · `ONLY A FEW BELIEVED.` · then, large: `CALL ANYWAY.`

segments.voice: The bell will give you two minutes. Think of one thing you keep doing that nobody notices. Washing the same dishes. Checking on a parent. Being the one who says good morning first. Praying when it feels like nobody's listening. Picture yourself doing it, the ordinary way you do. Don't ask whether it's working. Just see the faithfulness of it. If you pray, you can offer it to God as it is. If you don't, just let yourself be quietly proud of it for one minute. The bell holds the time.
Nuh, the prophet who called his people night and day for nine hundred and fifty years, while only a few listened.
Your line: call anyway. Today, keep going at one thing nobody notices. Do it once more, and do it well. Day twenty-nine.

howItsDone: Muslims honor Nuh as a prophet, and surah seventy-one, which bears his name, is read as a lesson in patient, persistent calling.

fork.setup: you've called your people for years. they put their fingers in their ears. what do you do?
options: give up; they've made their choice.
call again: night and day, openly and in private.
fork.reveal: he tried every way there was, for nine hundred and fifty years. the calling itself was the faithfulness.

original.note: Arabic: "a thousand years less fifty," the Qur'an's way of saying nine hundred and fifty (29:14).

trapdoor: what you thought: Noah, the ark, the animals.
what it means: nine hundred and fifty years — how long Nuh called his people, every way he could, while few listened.

what a scholar hears: 29:14 says a thousand years less fifty; scholars differ over how it maps onto his whole life; and surah seventy-one gives his own report of calling by night and day, openly and in private.

sources.quoted: he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years

sources.ref: Qur'an 71:5–12 (night and day; fingers in their ears; openly and in private; seek forgiveness)
Qur'an 11:40 (only a few believed with him)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4476 (the intercession: 'the first messenger to the people of the earth')

notes: Pickthall 29:14 quoted from memory ('And verily We sent Noah (as Our messenger) unto his folk, and he continued with them for a thousand years save fifty years; and the flood engulfed them, for they were wrong-doers.'). Confirm.

950 years: many take it as the length of his mission among his people; some commentators report further years before or after. The script says 'scholars differ over how it fits his whole life'. Confirm.
Bukhari 4476 (intercession): Nuh called 'the first of the messengers to the people of the earth' and 'a grateful servant' (17:3). Confirm.
Original: alfa sanatin illa khamsina 'aman (29:14); the Arabic uses two different words for year (sana, 'am). Confirm the vowelling.
